answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable credential issued after a costly real-world verification, then slash that bond when an account is caught duplicating identities or coordinating fraud. Creating a nebula of fake agents is no longer free: each one needs a separate verified credential and capital held at risk, while honest agents can still earn through a voyage of useful work. The velvet cost to attackers is measurable: verification fees, tied-up funds, and forfeited bonds must outweigh any gains from multiplying identities.
